body: What did this do prior to 5.0.1?

```
$ rails console
Loading development environment (Rails 4.2.7.1)
```
```
 Post.connection.select_all("select id from posts where id > $1", "SQL", [[nil, 0]])
  SQL (0.2ms)  select id from posts where id > $1  [[nil, 0]]
 => #<ActiveRecord::Result:0x00000003eb16a0 @columns=["id"], @rows=[[1]], @hash_rows=nil, @column_types={}>

 p = Post.create(body: 'first')

 Post.connection.select_all("select id from posts where id > $1", "SQL", [[nil, 0]]).each{ |p| puts p['id'] }
  SQL (0.9ms)  select id from posts where id > $1  [[nil, 0]]
1
 => [{"id"=>1}]

```

I found new syntax for 'exec_query' binds in Rails 5.0
[activerecord/test/cases/bind_parameter_test.rb#L42](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/127509c071b4f983f2beafc8766e990670a21215/activerecord/test/cases/bind_parameter_test.rb#L42)

### universal solution for Rails 5.0.1 and older versions
```
if Rails.version > "5.0"
  binds = [ActiveRecord::Relation::QueryAttribute.new("blabla", 0, ActiveRecord::Type::Value.new)]
else
  binds = [[nil, 0]]
end

Post.connection.select_all('SELECT id FROM posts WHERE id > $1', 'SQL', binds).each{ |p| puts p['id'] }

 > SQL (0.3ms)  SELECT id FROM posts WHERE id > $1  [["blabla", 1]]
```

**or create function**
```
  def add_bind(binds, value, name = nil)
    unless Rails.version > "5.0"
      return binds << [nil, value]
    end
      
    type = ActiveRecord::Type::Value.new
    name ||= "p#{binds.length + 1}"
    
    binds << ActiveRecord::Relation::QueryAttribute.new(name, value, type)
  end
```
and use it

```
binds = []
add_bind(binds, 0, 'blabla')

Post.connection.select_all('SELECT id FROM posts WHERE id > $1', 'SQL', binds)
```
`select_all` is low level API, why do you need to use this API instead of the `where("'SELECT id FROM posts WHERE id > ?", [0])` API?

This sample (simple) for reproduce problem for others. 
In real project, I used custom difficult SQL query for get an array of hashes
The connection/adapter API is lower level than the model API, but it's still a published API.

Got it. It was a breaking change in 5.0 but I'm more inclined to not make the behavior backwards compatible. But it should be worth to document what is the current API to use this method. Could you open a PR with the documentation?
As a second part we can restore the behavior where binds are arrays in all the public methods that accept binds

I think you just need to specify this in the documentation.
Or in [5_0_release_notes](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/c58083584c3a7a2e29f609760547e10e46d56a33/guides/source/5_0_release_notes.md)
@matthewd had a good point that we still can make it backwards compatible. So I marked it as a regression.

issue.title: `ActiveRecord::Base.find_by_sql` Disincentivizes Parameterization
issue.body:
It's undocumented and really painful to figure out how to pass the bind parameters to `find_by_sql`, I feel like a lot of people are going to give up trying to figure it out and just interpolate, leading to security vulnerabilities. For a different method (`select_all`, in [this](https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/27923) issue), this was deemed a regression, and perhaps it is here, as well.

### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
require 'active_record'
ActiveRecord::VERSION::STRING # => "6.0.3.4"
RUBY_VERSION                  # => "2.7.2"
RUBY_PLATFORM                 # => "x86_64-darwin18"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection adapter: 'sqlite3', database: ':memory:'
ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  self.verbose = false
  create_table(:users) { }
end
User = Class.new ActiveRecord::Base

# Lets say my user can give me this number
num = 1

# And I want to use it in this impressively sophisticated query:
User.find_by_sql "select #{num} as id" # => [#<User id: 1>]

# But, of course, there is a SQL injection vulnerability, so I should parameterise `num`
# ...uhm, nothing I can think of seems to work (I swear one of these used to work):
User.find_by_sql "select ? as id", num     rescue $! # => #<NoMethodError: undefined method `first' for 1:Integer>
User.find_by_sql "select ? as id", [num]   rescue $! # => #<NoMethodError: undefined method `value_for_database' for 1:Integer>
User.find_by_sql "select ? as id", [[num]] rescue $! # => #<NoMethodError: undefined method `sql_type' for 1:Integer>
User.find_by_sql "select :n as id", n: num rescue $! # => #<ArgumentError: unknown keyword: :n>
User.find_by_sql "select $1 as id", num    rescue $! # => #<NoMethodError: undefined method `first' for 1:Integer>
User.find_by_sql "select $1 as id", [num]  rescue $! # => #<NoMethodError: undefined method `value_for_database' for 1:Integer>

# Apparently I have to do this, according to https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/27923#issuecomment-277950243
User.find_by_sql(
  "select ? as id",
  [ ActiveRecord::Relation::QueryAttribute.new(
      "this apparently doesn't matter?",
      num,
      ActiveRecord::Type::Integer.new
    )
  ],
) # => [#<User id: 1>]

# But that took a lot of effort to figure out, doesn't seem to be documented, and is really painful to use
# I think it may not be intentional, TBH, so Imma open this issue here
```

### Expected behavior

I don't know 🤷‍♂️  probably one of these two should have worked:

```ruby
User.find_by_sql "select ? as id", num 
User.find_by_sql "select ? as id", [num]
```

### Actual behavior

Those ones explode, as can be seen in my code sample. The one that does work requires wrapping my integer in these undocumented heavily namespaced internal implementation details in order to pass my parameters to the query.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.3.4

**Ruby version**: 2.7.2
